name: Grape Manifest
summary: Milly Osworth needs you to bring her manifest to Brother Neals at Northshire Abbey. It will help the brotherhood replenish its wine stores.

sections.title: The Valley's Vintage
sections.body: Defias thieves and other brigands took the eastern fields. The abbey lost its food and its grapes. Milly has recovered the crop and recorded every bushel in her manifest, including what the occupied fields had yielded.

sections.title: A Tipple in the Belfry
sections.body: Brother Neals oversees food and drink at Northshire Abbey. In the quiet of the bell tower, he is known to sample Northshire's vintages. Brigands still threaten the gates, yet fresh grapes give the brotherhood a moment to toast the Light and take heart.

faq.answer: Milly Osworth records her harvest recovered from Defias thieves in the Grape Manifest. The ledger helps the abbey's quartermaster restock its cellars.
Brother Neals is a monk at Northshire Abbey who oversees its food and drink. He often samples the vintages in the bell tower.

faq.q: Where do I find Brother Neals?
faq.answer: Brother Neals is inside Northshire Abbey, in the bell tower overlooking the grounds.

faq.q: Why is Northshire's grape crop so important?
faq.answer: Northshire's grapes provide celebrated wine and fresh food for the local clergy and soldiers. A lost harvest threatens daily stores and the abbey's sacramental wine across Elwynn.
Defias brigands occupied Northshire Valley's eastern fields, drove Milly Osworth out, and hid her boxed harvest throughout the vineyards. Adventurers drove them back.

faq.q: What happens after giving Brother Neals the manifest?
faq.answer: Brother Neals gives his blessings in the name of the Light. He is overjoyed that the abbey's cellars will have fresh wine despite the bandit troubles across the valley.

angles.text: Securing Northshire's food stores helps Stormwind's main place of recruitment and recovery remain self-sufficient.
As a human beginning your journey, helping Milly and Brother Neals protects one of the kingdom's cherished pastoral traditions.
As a priest, you know wine has a place in hospitality and sacramental rites at Northshire Abbey, where farming sustains the brotherhood's worship.
